extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners preparing or evaluating Sequence Listing XML files for nucleotide and/or amino acid disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for preparing, formatting, submitting, and amending a Sequence Listing XML (WIPO ST.26) in U.S. patent applications that disclose nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: INSDQualifier 'id' attribute format and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualifier with a language-dependent free text value may be uniquely identified by using the optional XML attribute 'id' in the element INSDQualifier. The value of the 'id' attribute must start with the letter 'q' and continue with any positive integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The value of an 'id' attribute must be unique to one INSDQualifier element (i.e., used only once in a sequence listing file). (See paragraph 76 and paragraph 87(d) of WIPO Standard ST.26 as reproduced.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Organism qualifier content and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'organism' qualifier must disclose the source (single organism or origin) of the sequence and organism designations should be selected from a taxonomy database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the sequence is naturally occurring and the source organism has a Latin genus and species designation, that Latin designation must be used as the organism qualifier value. Preferred English common names may be specified only using the 'note' qualifier and must not be used as the organism qualifier value. If genus is known but species unspecified, indicate Latin genus followed by 'sp'. If genus and species designation is unknown, indicate 'unidentified' and place any known taxonomic information in the 'note' qualifier. If the source organism does not have a Latin genus/species (e.g., some viruses), use another acceptable scientific name (e.g., 'Canine adeno virus type 2'). If the sequence is not naturally occurring, indicate the organism qualifier value as 'synthetic construct' and provide further generation details in the 'note' qualifier. (WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 77–83.)

rubrics_metrics.name: mol_type qualifier allowed values
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'mol_type' qualifier must disclose the type of molecule represented in the sequence and differs from INSDSeq_moltype; nucleotide analogue sequences must be indicated as DNA or RNA and amino acid sequences as AA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nucleotide sequences the 'mol_type' qualifier value must be one of: 'genomic DNA', 'genomic RNA', 'mRNA', 'tRNA', 'rRNA', 'other RNA', 'other DNA', 'transcribed RNA', 'viral cRNA', 'unassigned DNA', or 'unassigned RNA'. If organism='synthetic construct', the 'mol_type' value must be either 'other RNA' or 'other DNA'. For amino acid sequences the 'mol_type' value is 'protein'. (WIPO ST.26 paragraph 84 and subparagraphs.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and length limit for free text values
rubrics_metrics.description: Free text is a type of value format for certain qualifiers presented as a descriptive text phrase or specified format (see controlled vocabulary in Annex I of ST.26).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of free text must be limited to a few short terms indispensable for understanding a characteristic of the sequence. For each qualifier other than the 'translation' qualifier, free text must not exceed 1000 characters. (WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 85–86.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Language-dependent free text: presentation and equivalence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Language-dependent free text qualifiers must present values in English and/or in a non-English element when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language-dependent free text must be presented in the INSDQualifier_value element in English, or in the NonEnglishQualifier_value element in another language, or both. If NonEnglishQualifier_value is present, the nonEnglishFreeTextLanguageCode attribute (ISO 639-1) must be specified in the root element and all NonEnglishQualifier_value elements must use that language. Where both NonEnglishQualifier_value and INSDQualifier_value are present for the same qualifier, the two must be equivalent: either NonEnglishQualifier_value is a translation of INSDQualifier_value, or vice versa, or both translate from the originalFreeTextLanguageCode. The INSDQualifier element may include optional attribute id (format 'q' followed by a positive integer) and must be unique. Technical terms and internationally used non-English proper names (e.g., 'in vitro') are considered English for INSDQualifier_value. (WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 85–87 and MPEP §2413.01(h).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifiers with language-dependent free text (Tables 5 and 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific qualifiers are identified as having language-dependent free text values and must follow the rules for language-dependent free text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nucleotide sequences (Table 5), qualifiers include: bound_moiety, cell_type, clone, clone_lib, collected_by, cultivar, dev_stage, ecotype, frequency, function, gene_synonym, haplogroup, host, identified_by, isolate, isolation_source, lab_host, mating_type, note, organism, phenotype, pop_variant, product, serotype, serovar, sex, standard_name, strain, sub_clone, sub_species, sub_strain, tissue_lib, tissue_type, variety, etc. For amino acid sequences (Table 6), qualifiers include: note and organism. (Reproduced from Annex I, Section 6 and 8 of WIPO ST.26 as in MPEP §2413.01(h).)

rubrics_metrics.name: CDS feature key and translation-related qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the 'CDS' feature key and associated qualifiers identifies coding sequences and their required annotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'CDS' feature's INSDFeature_location must include the stop codon. The 'transl_table' and 'translation' qualifiers may be used with 'CDS'; if 'transl_table' is not used, the Standard Code Table is assumed. The 'transl_except' qualifier must be used with 'CDS' and 'translation' to identify codons encoding pyrrolysine or selenocysteine. An amino acid sequence disclosed in a 'translation' qualifier that meets MPEP §2412.03's description must also be included in the sequence listing and assigned its own sequence identifier; that identifier must be provided as the value in the 'protein_id' qualifier with the 'CDS' feature key. The organism qualifier of the 'source' feature key for the amino acid sequence must be identical to that of its coding sequence. (WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 89–92.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Variant sequence inclusion and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary sequences and their variants must be included and properly represented in the sequence listing, each assigned sequence identifiers as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A primary sequence and any variant (each disclosed by enumeration and encompassed by MPEP §2412.03) must each be included and assigned its own sequence identifier. Variant sequences disclosed as a single sequence with enumerated alternative residues should be represented by a single sequence using the most restrictive ambiguity symbol. Variant sequences disclosed only by reference to deletions, insertions or substitutions should be included; representation rules: (a) may be annotated on the primary sequence where variations occur at a single or multiple distinct locations and occurrences are independent; (b) should be represented as a separate sequence with its own identifier where variations occur at multiple distinct locations and occurrences are interdependent; (c) must be a separate sequence and assigned an identifier where the inserted or substituted sequence contains in excess of 1000 residues. Symbols from WIPO/ST.26 Tables 1–4 should be used where appropriate; modified residues not in Tables require full unabbreviated names and further description in a feature table. (WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 93–100 and related MPEP references.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature key and qualifier rules for annotated variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotation of a specific variant must include a feature key, qualifier, and feature location, with constraints on 'replace' and 'note' qualifier values and formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The feature location and appropriate feature key/qualifier must be used for variant annotation. The 'replace' qualifier value must be only a single alternative nucleotide or nucleotide sequence using symbols from Table 1, or empty to indicate deletion. A listing of alternative residues can be given in the 'note' qualifier. If 'X' is used in a sequence to represent an unspecified amino acid, a listing of alternative amino acids must be provided in the 'note' qualifier. Values for 'replace' and 'note' are free text and must not exceed 1000 characters. Modified residues must be described fully and in a feature table per MPEP §§2412.05(b) and 2412.05(d). (WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 96–100 and MPEP §2413.01(g)/(h).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML file encoding, characters, and name rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sequence Listing XML' must be encoded using Unicode UTF-8, be in XML format, use permitted printable/nonprintable characters per WIPO ST.26, and follow file naming constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All characters must be encoded using Unicode UTF-8. The XML must use the permitted printable and non-printable (control) characters defined in WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 40 and 41 and Annex IV (Character Subset from Unicode Basic Latin). The file must be named *.xml (extension .xml), where the name (excluding extension) is 1–60 characters composed only of upper- or lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores; no spaces or other characters are permitted. The file must be compatible with PC or Mac computers and operating systems MS–DOS, MS–Windows, Mac OS, or Unix/Linux. (MPEP §2413.02 and WIPO ST.26 references.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML submission methods and file size/compression constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Options and constraints for submitting the Sequence Listing XML to the USPTO depending on file size and medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Sequence Listing XML must be in a single file and may be submitted either: (1) electronically via the USPTO patent electronic filing system (Patent Center) where file size must not exceed 100 MB and file compression is not permitted; or (2) on read-only optical disc(s) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e). For disc submissions: an uncompressed file must fit on a single disc; compression using WinZip, 7-Zip, or Unix/Linux Zip is permitted but compressed files must not be self-extracting; a compressed XML that does not fit on a single disc may be split into multiple file parts consistent with disc capacity and labeling rules. If the Sequence Listing XML is 100 MB or less, electronic submission via Patent Center is preferred. The Patent Center currently is the only USPTO system capable of accepting .xml files. Applicants should not submit both a Sequence Listing XML (ST.26) and a Sequence Listing that complies with ST.25 in the same submission; doing so will be rejected. (MPEP §§2413.03, 2413.03(b), 2413.03 and §2413.03 notes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of the Sequence Listing XML
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Sequence Listing XML is submitted, the specification generally must include an incorporation by reference paragraph identifying the XML file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless an exception applies (e.g., international applications during the international stage), when the Sequence Listing XML is submitted via e-filing or on read-only optical disc the specification must contain a separate paragraph (per §1.77(b)(5)) incorporating by reference the material in the XML file identifying: (i) the name of the file, (ii) the date of creation, and (iii) the size of the file in bytes. The incorporation by reference statement is required so the XML content is considered part of the disclosure capable of providing 35 U.S.C. 112(a) support for sequence-related claims. If the incorporation paragraph is omitted when required, pre-examination staff may issue a notice requiring a substitute specification or amendment to include the incorporation paragraph. Note: for international applications during the international phase, that incorporation paragraph is not required. (MPEP §2413.04 and discussion.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment requirements to add an initial Sequence Listing XML after filing (37 CFR 1.835(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment adding an initial Sequence Listing XML after the application filing date must include the XML and supporting statements and requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding an initial Sequence Listing XML after the filing date, the amendment must include: (1) a Sequence Listing XML in accordance with §§1.831–1.834 submitted as an XML file via Patent Center or on a read-only optical disc; (2) a request to amend the specification to include an incorporation by reference paragraph identifying file name, date of creation, and file size (except for international applications filed to the U.S. International Preliminary Examining Authority); (3) a statement indicating the basis for the amendment with specific references to parts of the originally filed application (specification, claims, drawings) for all sequence data in the XML; and (4) a statement that the Sequence Listing XML includes no new matter. Applicant responses to notices requiring an initial Sequence Listing XML should provide these items. (MPEP §2414.02(a) and related text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-examination and examiner checks, notices, and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-examination staff and examiners check for formal compliance with sequence listing rules; missing or defective Sequence Listing XMLs will generate notices and requirements to cure deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-examination staff check that applications with sequence disclosures comply with 37 CFR 1.831–1.835 and will issue notifications if a compliant Sequence Listing XML is missing or defective. The examiner may require filing or replacement of a Sequence Listing XML (e.g., if sequences in the disclosure are not part of the XML of record). Notices will identify deficiencies and provide instructions and time to comply; failure to timely comply may lead to abandonment. When an amendment is required to add or replace a Sequence Listing XML in response to a notice, it must conform to the procedural requirements of 37 CFR 1.835 (amendment to add initial file or to replace). The grant of a patent on such an application creates a presumption that the granted patent complies with the sequence rules, and neither presence nor absence of non-required information creates a presumption of necessity for 35 U.S.C. 112 requirements. (MPEP §§2413.05, 2414, 2414.01–2414.03 discussions.)
